citeAs: Rohatgi, S., Qin, Y., Aw, B., Unnithan, N., Kan, M.-Y. (2023). The ACL OCL Corpus: Advancing Open Science in Computational Linguistics. arXiv:2305.14996.
creator: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan (Pennsylvania State University; National University of Singapore)
description: ACL OCL is a scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology, containing 73,285 papers in the Computational Linguistics domain published from 1952 to September 2022. It provides structured full texts with sections, figures, citation graphs, enriched metadata, and links to the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph. The corpus also includes 210K extracted figures and model-predicted topic labels for each paper.
name: ACL OCL
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Topic labels were obtained by crawling published papers from online CL conferences (ACL 2020, EMNLP 2020, ACL-IJCNLP 2021, EACL 2021, NAACL 2021) along with their author-submitted topic labels from conference websites. A PLM-based supervised model (SPECTER) was then trained on 2,545 labeled papers and used to predict silver topic labels for all OCL papers.
rai:dataBiases: The corpus is limited to peer-reviewed CL papers from the ACL Anthology, which may underrepresent low-resource languages. Prior research found that numerous languages remain underrepresented in the ACL Anthology. The distribution of top-cited papers is biased towards dominant topics (e.g., Machine Translation), which affects topic classification accuracy.
rai:dataCollection: The corpus was built by crawling PDF files and metadata from the ACL Anthology website. PDF files longer than 50 pages (mostly conference volume introductions or handbooks) were removed. Full texts were extracted from PDFs using GROBID. Figures and tables were extracted using PDFFigures. The corpus was then enriched by linking to the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph (S2AG) via its Graph API.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Full-text extraction fails mostly for papers between the years 2000 to 2015 (as shown in Figure 2). Only 16.8% of OCL papers have an arXiv paper ID. Some fields are only valid for a portion of papers.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: PDF files and metadata from the ACL Anthology website, covering 73,285 conference, journal, and workshop papers in the Computational Linguistics domain.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection
rai:dataLimitations: The OCL corpus is a small-scale collection focusing only on peer-reviewed and open-access CL papers from the ACL Anthology, not including other sources. Full-text extraction quality is limited by GROBID's constraints (missing sections, merged paragraphs, footnote mixing, table/figure extraction errors). Only open-source PDF extraction tools were used due to budget constraints. The corpus is an unlabeled resource lacking annotations for specific tasks.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF files longer than 50 pages were removed. Full texts were extracted from PDFs using GROBID, adopting the S2ORC-JSON format. Figures and tables were extracted using PDFFigures (Clark and Divvala, 2016). Language detection was applied using a public language detection toolkit (langdetect) with title and abstract as inputs. The corpus was linked to Semantic Scholar Academic Graph via its Graph API using ACL Anthology IDs.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset undergoes annual updates to keep it current with the ACL Anthology. New additions are identified by monitoring changes in URLs. The ultimate plan is to provide full-text extraction and information extraction APIs to ACL Anthology, hosting the OCL data on ACL Anthology itself.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The corpus advances open science in computational linguistics by providing accessible and standardized data resources, promoting reproducibility in research. It enables analysis of research trends including the emergence of ethics-related topics in NLP and the representation of low-resource languages in the CL community.
rai:dataUseCases: Temporal topic trend analysis; document-level information extraction; related work generation; figure caption generation; pre-training or fine-tuning scientific language models; knowledge graph construction; bibliographic and metadata analysis; historical language change analysis; paper-reviewer matching; multimodal research tasks combining text and figures.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GROBID (for full-text extraction from PDFs); PDFFigures (Clark and Divvala, 2016) for figure and table extraction; langdetect (Shuyo, 2010) for language detection; SPECTER and SciBERT PLM-based models for topic classification (silver labels); BART-large-MNLI for zero-shot and semi-supervised topic classification.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: No human annotation per item; topic labels are machine-predicted silver labels from author-submitted conference topics, not multiple independent human annotations per paper.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: No human annotators used; topic labels are derived from author-submitted conference metadata and machine-predicted silver labels.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No inter-annotator agreement or human annotation quality analysis reported; topic classification is evaluated via model accuracy metrics (Macro F1, Weighted F1, Accuracy) not annotation agreement.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No annotation platform used; topic labels come from author-submitted conference metadata and automated model predictions.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol described for missing data; missing fields are left absent rather than imputed.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No post-collection data manipulation such as augmentation, balancing, or resampling described for the dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The corpus contains scholarly papers with author names and metadata; no sensitive personal information is discussed or collected beyond standard academic publication metadata.

evidence.name: We present ACL OCL, a scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist Open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain.
evidence.description: The OCL corpus includes 73,285 papers hosted by the ACL Anthology published from 1952 to September 2022. The OCL further provides higher-quality structured full texts for all papers, instead of previous string-formatted ones, enabling richer textual analyses.
evidence.url: Our dataset is available from HuggingFace. https://huggingface.co/datasets/WINGNUS/ACL-OCL

evidence.inLanguage: Figure 3 illustrates the distribution of the top 27 out of 96 languages within the corpus. As expected, English is the most dominant language processed in the ACL OCL. However, it is noteworthy that languages such as Latin and Gujarati are also present.

evidence.isLiveDataset: The dataset undergoes annual updates, during which we download and process papers recently added to the ACL Anthology. We plan to update OCL by year to keep it alive.
evidence.rai:dataCollection: We start by crawling the PDF files and metadata from the source ACL Anthology. We then pass the PDF files through the full-text extraction process. We enhance this data using Semantic Scholar's API to fetch additional information about OCL papers.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionType: From the ACL Anthology, we design crawlers to fetch all the PDF documents and metadata from its website. Meta information is included, as the website's version is more accurate than that obtained by PDF extraction, given its author-driven nature.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The OCL corpus includes 73,285 papers hosted by the ACL Anthology published from 1952 to September 2022.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionRawData: From the ACL Anthology, we design crawlers to fetch all the PDF documents and metadata from its website. We then obtain 73,285 conference journal and workshop papers in the CL domain.
evidence.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: We remove PDF files longer than 50 pages, which are mostly conference volume introductions or handbooks. We use GROBID for the full-text extraction from PDF files. We take the S2ORC-JSON format used by Lo et al. (2020) and Wang et al. (2020) for our full-text schema, which includes complete information parsed from PDF files, such as metadata, authors, and body text with citations, references, sections and etc.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: We observe that our full-text extraction fail mostly for papers between the years 2000 to 2015. We note that certain fields are only valid on a portion of the papers. For example, only 16.8% of OCL papers have arxiv_paper_id, indicating a corresponding version in arXiv.org.
evidence.rai:dataLimitations: The OCL corpus is a small-scale collection of documents specifically focusing on peer-reviewed and open-access CL papers. As a result, it is not a comprehensive corpus like S2ORC (Lo et al., 2020), since it does not include any other sources beyond the ACL Anthology. Due to constraints on budget, only open-source toolkits are considered, although it is acknowledged that some paid PDF2text services might yield higher-quality full texts.
evidence.rai:dataUseCases: By nature, ACL OCL is a scholarly corpus aiming to enable and benefit a wide range of research. Additional forms of topic analyses and topic-aided tasks are now feasible with the domain-specific, fine-grained topic information provided by OCL, such as emerging topic detection, evolution detection of topics, paper-reviewer matching via topics.
evidence.rai:dataSocialImpact: Building scholarly corpora for open research accelerates scientific progress and promotes reproducibility in research by providing researchers with accessible and standardized data resources. We ask for more attention on the emerging new topics such as "Ethics of NLP" and the declining underrepresented topics like "Discourse and Pragmatics" and "Phonology, Morphology and Word Segmentation".
evidence.rai:dataBiases: Prior research (Ranathunga and de Silva, 2022) on the representation of low-resource languages in the ACL Anthology found that numerous languages remain underrepresented. The 87% accuracy is higher than an expected 69% accuracy tested on the STop test set in Table 5, mainly because of the bias in the distribution of top-cited papers towards dominant topics (e.g., MT).
evidence.rai:machineAnnotationTools: We use GROBID for the full-text extraction from PDF files. We extract figures and tables from PDF files using PDFFigures (Clark and Divvala, 2016). To detect the language in which a document is written, we utilize a public language detection toolkit (Shuyo, 2010) with its title and abstract as inputs.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: We crawl published papers of several online held CL conferences (e.g., ACL 2020, EACL 2021) between 2020 and 2022, together with their topics from those websites. After aligning those papers with the data in the ACL OCL, we obtained 2545 documents classified in 21 topics in total.
evidence.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset undergoes annual updates, during which we download and process papers recently added to the ACL Anthology. For these updates, we identify new additions by monitoring changes in URLs. We plan to update OCL by year to keep it alive. The ultimate solution is to provide full-text extraction and information extraction APIs to ACL Anthology, thus hosting the OCL data on ACL Anthology itself.
